title: SPC700 greedy allocation asserts on a copy hint outside the allocation order
summary: On upstream main 06bc967d2668 with assertions, -mcpu=mosspc700 -O2 aborts in the Greedy Register Allocator with "Target hint is outside allocation order" on 18 of the 52 corpus IRs of the series' default-mode set (boids, bf-vm, cardioid, mvscrl, ...). MOSRegisterInfo::getRegAllocationHints offers a strong copy hint that the SPC700 allocation order of the class does not contain. Upstream plus #584 still aborts the same way. The #320 split's 1c commit filters a strong hint that is not in the order (added for the empty Imag32 order on non-65816 CPUs); on SPC700 that turns this assertion into "ran out of registers during register allocation" followed by an abort in the Virtual Register Rewriter, so the inputs still fail. Not fixed; root cause in the SPC700 orders not traced.
attribution: Found by the third-round all-CPU default-mode gate of the #320/#321 split; evidence and this record: Claude Code 2.1.285 t4-opus-high agent a7633adfeee82a4f5, model Claude Opus 5.5 (claude-opus-5-5), high reasoning effort (agent definition); session 310aee67-a99e-4b78-ba48-c560322fe80d (https://claude.ai/code/session_01Skyq488smgqkyyzHrcCX7F).
unknowns: Not reduced; which register class and hint trigger it is not traced.
Release builds were not examined; without the assertion the allocator may proceed with an out-of-order hint.

search_terms: Target hint is outside allocation order
prior_work.source_assessment: Upstream getRegAllocationHints returns a strong hint without checking that it is in Order; 1c adds `is_contained(Order, *StrongHint)`.
prior_work.binary_assessment: p-321-00 and r3-584-up abort with the signature; r3-320-1b too; r3-320-1c and the series top fail with an out-of-registers error and a rewriter abort instead.
prior_work.decision: New defect, upstream; distinct from the late-opt crash (different pass, still present after #584).
